messages:
nina-ml: Nightly eval flagged a regression on rdx-13b-quant-v2 — duplication/streaks spiked on the summarization prompt set. Seen across CPU/GPU runs. Attaching a couple example outputs and quick stats from the job :eyes:

nina-ml: Nightly delta: duplication-rate 3.8% -> 8.2% (relative +116%). failing prompt subset id: summarizer_v2_2026. Run id: nightly-20260318-07

nina-ml: Example generation (seed=20260318, commit=a1f9b2c - runtime/optimize-rng-kernel):
```
Prompt: "Summarize the following research paragraph..."
Output: "The study finds that the the the the the approach is promising. the the the..."
```

frank-runtime: ugh. can you paste the exact infer command and seed? any differences in batching config vs baseline run? :bug:

nina-ml: Command I used:
```
infer --model rdx-13b-quant-v2 --commit a1f9b2c --prompt-file prompts/summarizer_v2.txt --max-tokens 128 --seed 20260318 --batch 8 --continuous-batch true
```
Baseline commit that was fine: runtime/merge/20260310 (commit: 9c4d8e7)

ben-ops: I merged the `optimize-rng-kernel` PR on 2026-03-16. It changes how RNG state is stored when we do kernel-level microbatches. Could be a shared-state bug for continuous batching.

eva-q: Also pushed a small attention index change same day (attn-index-fix). But that shouldn't affect sampling randomness. Still worth checking logits shape diffs.

sam-rl: quick idea — run deterministic sampling harness: single-worker, no continuous batching, same seed across commits. If outputs diverge then RNG is different. If logits differ before sampling then attention/kernel change impacted forward pass.

nina-ml: I ran a quick deterministic compare (no continuous batching): differences are smaller, duplication only up ~1%. With continuous batching enabled duplication spikes. So leaning RNG state handling when microbatching is on.

frank-runtime: ok that points at the kernel RNG state change. Can you reproduce with minimal script that does two back-to-back samples inside same process (simulate continuous batching) vs separate processes? If same-process reproduces, we can bisect the RNG code.

nina-ml: repro script attached (snippet):
```
# single process, two inferences without reinit
infer --model rdx-13b-quant-v2 --seed 42 --prompt p1
infer --model rdx-13b-quant-v2 --seed 42 --prompt p2
# vs
# separate process: same commands but run fresh process for each
```

frank-runtime: I ran that locally against a1f9b2c, and got repeated token streaks in the second inference. Against 9c4d8e7 it looks normal. So RNG carryover bug confirmed.

ben-ops: Found the offending diff in a1f9b2c: we moved RNG state into a thread_local static inside the kernel to avoid reallocation. We forgot to re-seed on session boundary when continuous-batch reuses worker threads. Patch incoming.

eva-q: We should also add a unit test in nightly-evals: run two sequential inferences with same seed and assert identical per-token logits vs baseline. If RNG persists incorrectly, logits will differ.

sam-rl: I'll add a regression test to sampling-harness. Also add a small synthetic prompt set to stress duplication cases.

leo: For mitigation, can we add a hotfix that forces RNG reseed on request boundary for continuous-batch workers? Prefer that while patch is reviewed.

frank-runtime: agreed. I'll PR `rng: reseed_on_request` to the runtime and stage a canary on dev-dedicated for 2 hours. If canary looks good, roll to nightly pipeline.

nina-ml: CI bot posted the failing job: <https://ci.internal.redwood/nightly/20260318-07>

ci-bot: nightly-evals alert — job nightly-20260318-07: regression detected on summarizer_v2_2026. Duplication-rate increased from 3.8% to 8.2%. Investigating: @nina-ml @frank-runtime

ben-ops: PR link: https://git.internal.redwood/runtime/pull/548 (hotfix + unit tests)

frank-runtime: running canary now (deploy id: canary-20260318-rng-fix). Will post quick metrics in 20m.

nina-ml: Thanks — if canary looks good I'll kick a full nightly re-run. Also flagging customer-impact: small subset of generation-based features might see hallucination-like repeats; CS pinged.

leo: If we revert a1f9b2c entirely, we lose the microbatch allocation perf win. So prefer targeted reseed fix + tests and then re-evaluate microbatch RNG approach.

frank-runtime: Canary results: duplication-rate dropped back to 3.9% on canary pool. Looks promising :thumbsup:

nina-ml: Great — please merge hotfix and cut a patch release. I'll schedule a full nightly re-run after merge and monitor.

sam-rl: Action items:
- frank-runtime: merge hotfix + rollout (done after checks)
- ben-ops: add unit/regression tests to runtime
- sam-rl: update sampling-harness and add stress prompts
- nina-ml: run full nightly re-eval and post final metrics

frank-runtime: merged and rolled to nightly (release: runtime-20260318-patch1). Please validate.

nina-ml: Re-run finished: duplication-rate now 3.85% (within noise). Closing regression. Thanks everyone :tada:
